henri_lefebvre.identity_note: Author of La production de l’espace (Anthropos, 1974), identified as Henri Lefebvre (1901–1991) in BnF record FRBNF35199294; English translation credited to Donald Nicholson-Smith by CiNii Books BA12992226. weber.title: Stanford Encyclopedia: Max Weber
weber.citation: Sung Ho Kim, “Max Weber,” Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy (2007; substantive revision 2022; consulted updated online entry).

verification.note: Read sections 1, 2, 3 and 4.1 completely; only opening of 4.2, not sections 5–6. Supports the historical-economics milieu/Schmoller commission, selective Rickert reception, Marianne’s editorial role and disputed unity of posthumous Economy and Society. This is a scholarly interpretation; questionable incidental chronology and evaluative political phrasing are not adopted.

benjamin_history_primary.title: Walter Benjamin, “On the Concept of History” (1940), trans. Dennis Redmond (2005).
benjamin_history_primary.citation: Walter Benjamin, “On the Concept of History” (1940), trans. Dennis Redmond (2005).

verification.note: Primary translation sections II–IX checked for remembrance, inheritance and the critique of progress. The translation is Redmond’s, not Harry Zohn’s; the archive identifies a 1974 German collected edition. The text alone does not establish later reception: Winter’s separate conclusion opening supplies the specific use recorded here. No whole Frankfurt School doctrine is inferred. Expanded check: complete theses I–XVIII and A/B plus translator note now read. Original German witness remains uncollated; translation choices and political/civilizational judgments remain attributed. Named Nietzsche XII and Fustel VII passages support the new links.

marx_1859_preface.title: Karl Marx, preface to A Contribution to the Critique of Political Economy (1859), reproduced from Progress Publishers 1977.
marx_1859_preface.citation: Karl Marx, preface to A Contribution to the Critique of Political Economy (1859), reproduced from Progress Publishers 1977.

verification.note: Read complete primary preface body. Supports Marx’s account of forces/relations, forms in which people fight out conflicts, critical reexamination of Hegel and collaboration with Engels. The strong developmental propositions are attributed theoretical claims. Later website endnotes about an Asiatic mode or Engels’s interpretation are not adopted as Marx’s 1859 text; original edition uncollated.

weber_method_primary.title: Max Weber, methodological foundations of sociology and excerpt from “Objectivity” in social science (1904), reproduced from Sociological Writings, edited by Wolf Heydebrand (1994).
weber_method_primary.citation: Max Weber, methodological foundations of sociology and excerpt from “Objectivity” in social science (1904), reproduced from Sociological Writings, edited by Wolf Heydebrand (1994).

verification.note: Read all available Definition of Sociology and Methodological Foundations sections 1–11, and the entire displayed Objectivity excerpt; clipped passages were reread locally. These are excerpts, not the complete original works. Supports meaning and causal evidence, ideal types, value-relevant selection without arbitrary validity, and criticism of a juristic refutation of materialist history. Particular Meyer counterfactual use is explicit. Historical racial/animal asides are not adopted; original German and edition history uncollated.

marx_colonisation_primary.title: Karl Marx, Capital, volume I (1867), chapter33, The Modern Theory of Colonisation, English transcription.
marx_colonisation_primary.citation: Karl Marx, Capital, volume I (1867), chapter33, The Modern Theory of Colonisation, English transcription.

verification.note: Complete chapter body and notes1–16 read; later notes not fully read. Marx criticizes Wakefield’s restriction of access to land as producing dependence on wage labour. The chapter does not name Mill: comparison with Mill’s endorsement of Wakefield is editorially established from both texts, not a claimed direct Marx-to-Mill quotation. Marx’s own settler and virgin-soil framing does not supply a complete Indigenous account of dispossession. No full Capital reading or edition collation claimed.

dc165_lefebvre_excerpt_1974.title: Henri Lefebvre, “La production de l’espace,” L’Homme et la société 31–32 (1974): 15–32, DOI 10.3406/homso.1974.1855; excerpt from the book’s introduction.
dc165_lefebvre_excerpt_1974.citation: Henri Lefebvre, “La production de l’espace,” L’Homme et la société 31–32 (1974): 15–32, DOI 10.3406/homso.1974.1855; excerpt from the book’s introduction.

verification.note: Primary excerpt pp. 15–32 read. The official Persée rendering supplied p. 15 and its note identifying an extract from the newly published Anthropos book; a Rhuthmos mirror of the same Persée scan supplied the remaining readable OCR, https://www.rhuthmos.eu/IMG/pdf/henri_lefebvre_la_production_de_l_espace_1974.pdf. Locators: pp. 19–20 reject inventories and purely textual decoding as sufficient explanations; pp. 21–22 discuss capitalism, hegemony and space’s active role; pp. 25–27 seek the processes producing spaces and their codes. Complete French monograph and English translation body unread. Interpretations of Hegel, Marx and other writers in the excerpt remain Lefebvre’s arguments, without new person-to-person arrows.
